body: Which method is the entry point of a standalone Java program?
explanation: The JVM starts a program by calling public static void main(String[] args).

body: Which keyword creates a new object?
explanation: new allocates an object and calls its constructor, e.g. new Scanner(System.in).
Dividing two ints performs integer division and drops the decimal part.

body: Which primitive type stores true or false?
explanation: Java's primitive is boolean. bool is used in C# and C++, not Java.

body: What must end most Java statements?
explanation: Statements such as declarations and method calls end with a semicolon.

body:
What does this print?

System.out.println("Java".length());
explanation: length() returns the number of characters: J, a, v, a.

body: Which line correctly creates an array of 5 integers?
explanation: Java arrays are created with new and a size. The variable type must be int[].

body: How does Java code usually run?
options: It runs only inside web browsers
It is compiled straight to a Windows .exe only
It is compiled to bytecode, which runs on the JVM
explanation: javac compiles source into bytecode (.class files), and the Java Virtual Machine runs that bytecode on any platform.

body:
What does this print?

System.out.println(10 % 3);
explanation: % gives the remainder: 10 = 3 * 3 + 1.

body: Which keyword makes a class inherit from another class?
explanation: A class extends one parent class and implements interfaces.
== checks whether both refer to the same object; new String creates a separate object. equals() compares the characters.

body:
What does this print?

System.out.println(1 + 2 + "3");
explanation: Evaluation goes left to right: 1 + 2 = 3 (numbers), then 3 + "3" joins as text to give "33".

body:
What does this print?

System.out.println("3" + 1 + 2);
explanation: The string comes first, so each + joins text: "3" + 1 = "31", then "31" + 2 = "312".

body: Which access modifier makes a member visible only inside its own class?
explanation: private members cannot be accessed from any other class. No modifier means package-level access.

options: An ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException is thrown at runtime
explanation: Valid indexes are 0, 1 and 2. Accessing index 3 fails at runtime.
i++ uses the current value (5) and then increments, so the next read of i gives 6.

body: Which statement about interfaces and abstract classes is true?
options: A class can extend several classes
A class can implement many interfaces but extend only one class
Abstract classes cannot contain any method bodies
explanation: Java allows single class inheritance and multiple interface implementation. Abstract classes may have both abstract and concrete methods.

body: Which collection does NOT allow duplicate elements?
explanation: A Set stores each element at most once. Lists and deques keep duplicates.
substring(1, 4) starts at index 1 and stops before index 4: characters 1, 2, 3 = "hen".

body: What is method overloading?
options: A subclass replacing a parent method with the same signature
Calling a method many times in a loop
Several methods with the same name but different parameter lists
explanation: Overloading is decided at compile time by the parameters. Replacing a parent method is overriding; a method calling itself is recursion.
When i reaches 3, break exits the loop before printing.

options: Compile-time error: a final variable cannot be reassigned
It throws an exception at runtime
explanation: The compiler rejects any assignment to a final variable after it has been initialised.
Overridden methods are chosen at runtime from the actual object type (B), not the variable type (A).
Autoboxing reuses cached Integer objects from -128 to 127, so a and b are the same object; 128 creates new objects. Compare values with equals().
f computes the factorial: 5 * 4 * 3 * 2 * 1 = 120.
The finally block runs before the method actually returns, so "F " is printed before println prints the returned 1.
Strings are immutable. toUpperCase() returns a new string, which is discarded here; s is unchanged.

body: What happens when you put a key that already exists into a HashMap?
options: Both values are stored under the key
The old value is replaced by the new value
explanation: Keys are unique. put() overwrites the existing value and returns the old one.
A static field is shared by all objects of the class, so each constructor call increments the same counter.

body: Which exception must be either caught or declared with throws?
explanation: IOException is a checked exception. The others extend RuntimeException (unchecked), so the compiler does not force you to handle them.
